description: Remote Config validation vectors (ARCH §7, §13; SPEC AC-020, AC-293). Single source of truth for web/src/core/routing.test.ts (Vitest) and the iOS RemoteConfigService XCTest port (ARCH §19.3; SPEC §10.7, AC-168). T-060 wrote the `routingPolicy` section (D-96); T-102 adds one sibling section per other RC key.

conventions: Input forms: {"absent": true} = no RC value yet; {"notString": v} = a non-string value (web only: an iOS RemoteConfigValue is always a string, so iOS skips these); {"raw": s} = this exact string; {"edits": [...]} = apply the edits in order to a deep copy of `default`, then serialise it as compact JSON; {"padTo": n} = compact `default` with spaces inserted before its final "}" until it is n characters long; {"repeat": {"text": t, "times": n}} = t repeated n times.

An edit is {"path": [keys], "value": v} (set, creating the key if missing) or {"path": [keys], "delete": true}. No path segment is ever "__proto__"; those cases are raw strings, because assigning "__proto__" in JavaScript sets the prototype instead of a key.

expect.warning is the exact warning string, or null. The reason is not_string, too_large, invalid_json, bad_shape, bad_version, unknown_enum or floor. Paths are listed classes S0..S4, fields web, ios, noModel, cloud, then jobs in `jobs` order, and never echo RC text.

expect.policy is "default" (the bundled policy) or {"edits": [...]} applied to a deep copy of `default`. Every reason except floor means the bundled policy as a whole (no partial merge, D-84); floor keeps the bundled value only for each listed entry.
Lengths are in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string length); every case here is ASCII except the BOM, zero-width-space and Cyrillic cases, which fail before the length matters.
